alt: Dominoes placed one at a time on a small board whose squares show (row + col) % 2. Every domino covers one square showing 0 and one showing 1, so the covered count stays balanced. On a board with two opposite corners removed, the squares showing 1 outnumber those showing 0, so two squares are always left over.

steps.caption: A 4 by 4 board with corners (0, 0) and (3, 3) removed. Each square shows (row + col) % 2. 14 squares remain: 6 show 0 and 8 show 1.
Domino 1 covers (0, 1) and (0, 2), which show 1 and 0: one of each. So far 1 square showing 0 and 1 showing 1 are covered.
Domino 2 covers (0, 3) and (1, 3), which show 1 and 0: one of each. So far 2 squares showing 0 and 2 showing 1 are covered.
Domino 3 covers (1, 0) and (1, 1), which show 1 and 0: one of each. So far 3 squares showing 0 and 3 showing 1 are covered.
Domino 4 covers (1, 2) and (2, 2), which show 1 and 0: one of each. So far 4 squares showing 0 and 4 showing 1 are covered.
Domino 5 covers (2, 0) and (2, 1), which show 0 and 1: one of each. So far 5 squares showing 0 and 5 showing 1 are covered.
Domino 6 covers (3, 0) and (3, 1), which show 1 and 0: one of each. So far 6 squares showing 0 and 6 showing 1 are covered.

No domino fits any more, leaving (2, 3) and (3, 2) with no partner. Every domino covers one 0 and one 1, but this board has 6 zeros and 8 ones, so the surplus squares cannot be covered by any placement, not only this one.
